name: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)
summary: Subsidies for growing fruits and vegetables: new orchards, hybrid vegetable cultivation, polyhouses, nurseries, and post-harvest facilities like cold storage and pack houses.

benefits.headline: Roughly 35% to 50% subsidy on horticulture projects (varies by component)
details: Area expansion (new orchards, hybrid vegetables): typically around 40% of the approved cost, with ceilings per hectare.
Protected cultivation such as polyhouses and shade-net houses: up to 50% for vegetables and flowers.
Post-harvest infrastructure such as cold storage, cold rooms and pack houses: roughly 35% to 50% of the project cost.
Assistance for rejuvenating old orchards, plastic mulching, nurseries and organic farming.

summary: Farmers growing horticulture crops (fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, plantation crops). SHGs, FPOs and cooperatives can also apply.
Each component has its own ceilings and conditions, set by your State Horticulture Mission.

steps: Meet your District Horticulture Officer (or State Horticulture Mission office) and ask which components are open for your crop.
Apply on the state horticulture portal or submit the form at the district office, with documents and (for projects) a project report.
Wait for sanction before you start work or purchase. Begin only after approval.
After inspection of the completed work, the subsidy is credited to your bank account (project loans may be bank-linked).

deadline.text: No national last date. Components open according to state annual action plans, so ask your Horticulture office when applications open.

caveats: Percentages are indicative national patterns. Always confirm the exact rate for your component with your district Horticulture office.
